title: Three Tokens, One Failure Domain
description: A ring places three replicas on the next three virtual tokens. An audit finds all three tokens sometimes belong to one physical server. Which correction matters most?

options.text: Count virtual tokens as independent servers in availability estimates.
options.explanation: One physical failure removes all tokens on that server, so the copies share a failure domain.

options.text: Increase virtual tokens without changing replica selection.
options.explanation: More tokens may improve balance but still allow multiple replicas on the same machine.

options.text: Switch to modulo hashing while retaining the same placement rule.
options.explanation: Changing key routing does not by itself enforce independent replica placement and increases churn-related movement.

options.text: Skip tokens on already-chosen physical nodes when selecting replicas.
options.explanation: Replica selection must use distinct physical nodes, with topology constraints where required. Virtual tokens help balance ownership, not provide independent durability.
